quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 4 lines of symmetry, matching its 4 equal sides?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Think about the shape you can fold in half four different ways and still have both sides match.
quests.explanation: A square has exactly 4 lines of symmetry: straight down the middle two ways, and corner to corner two ways.
quests.funFact: For many regular shapes, the number of lines of symmetry matches the number of sides.

quests.instruction: Which shape has more lines of symmetry than any other shape — so many that you could never count them all?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Think about the shape you could fold in half through the middle, in any direction at all.
quests.explanation: A circle has infinite lines of symmetry — you can fold it in half through the center any way you like.
quests.funFact: No matter which line you draw through a circle's center, both halves always match perfectly.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 3 lines of symmetry, matching its 3 equal sides?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: Think about the shape you can fold in half three different ways, once from each corner.
quests.explanation: A triangle with equal sides has exactly 3 lines of symmetry, one running from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
quests.funFact: Just like the square, this triangle's lines of symmetry match its number of equal sides.

quests.instruction: Which shape has more lines of symmetry than a rectangle, even though both have 4 sides?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Think about which 4-sided shape has all of its sides perfectly equal.
quests.explanation: A square has 4 lines of symmetry, more than a rectangle's 2, because all of a square's sides are equal.
quests.funFact: Equal sides are the secret behind extra lines of symmetry.

quests.instruction: Which shape's lines of symmetry can never be fully counted, no matter how long you try?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Think about the one shape with truly endless lines of symmetry.
quests.explanation: A circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry, so counting them all is impossible.
quests.funFact: Every single line drawn through a circle's exact center creates two matching halves.

quests.instruction: Square, Triangle, Square, Triangle, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: This pattern swaps between Square and Triangle every single time.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Square, Triangle, so after Square comes Triangle again.
quests.funFact: Once you spot which two shapes are alternating, the rest of the pattern is easy to predict.

quests.instruction: Circle, Square, Circle, Square, Circle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Look at how Circle and Square keep taking turns — which one comes right after Circle?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Circle, Square, so after Circle comes Square again.
quests.funFact: Patterns that alternate between two shapes are some of the simplest to predict.

quests.instruction: Which shape has more lines of symmetry than a hexagon, a pentagon, and an octagon all put together?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Think about the one shape whose symmetry can never truly be beaten by any polygon.
quests.explanation: A circle's infinite lines of symmetry beat any polygon, no matter how many sides it has.
quests.funFact: As a regular polygon gains more and more sides, it starts to look more like a circle.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 5 lines of symmetry, just like a pentagon, even though it has sharp points instead of plain sides?
quests.question: Star
quests.hint: Think about the pointy shape with the same symmetry count as a pentagon.
quests.explanation: A classic 5-pointed star has exactly 5 lines of symmetry, just like a pentagon.
quests.funFact: That's no coincidence — a pentagon shape is actually hidden at the center of every classic star.

quests.instruction: Diamond, Square, Square, Diamond, Square, Square, Diamond, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Diamond, Square, Square over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Diamond, Square, Square, so after Diamond, Square comes another Square.
quests.funFact: Breaking a long pattern into its repeating group makes it much easier to predict.

quests.instruction: Circle, Circle, Triangle, Circle, Circle, Triangle, Circle, Circle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of three: Circle, Circle, Triangle — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Circle, Circle, Triangle, so after two circles comes a triangle.
quests.funFact: Patterns can repeat groups of three or more shapes, not just two.

quests.instruction: Star, Circle, Star, Circle, Star, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Follow the back-and-forth between Star and Circle to find what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Star, Circle, so after Star comes Circle again.
quests.funFact: An alternating pattern always repeats the same two shapes in the same order.

quests.instruction: Triangle, Square, Square, Triangle, Square, Square, Triangle, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Break this into groups of Triangle, Square, Square to spot what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Triangle, Square, Square. The sequence just gave Triangle, Square — so the group finishes with another Square.
quests.funFact: Once you know a pattern repeats every three shapes, you can predict any position in the sequence.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 1 line of symmetry, running straight down the middle?
quests.question: Heart
quests.hint: Think about the shape you can only fold in half one single way, top to bottom.
quests.explanation: A heart has just 1 line of symmetry, straight down the middle, matching its left and right halves.
quests.funFact: Try folding a paper heart down the center — the two sides will match perfectly.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 6 lines of symmetry, matching its 6 equal sides?
quests.question: Hexagon
quests.hint: Think about the shape with one more line of symmetry than a pentagon.
quests.explanation: A regular hexagon has exactly 6 lines of symmetry, matching its 6 equal sides.
quests.funFact: Honeycomb hexagons are naturally very balanced, which is part of why bees build with this shape.

quests.instruction: Rectangle, Rectangle, Square, Rectangle, Rectangle, Square, Rectangle, Rectangle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of three: Rectangle, Rectangle, Square — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Rectangle, Rectangle, Square. The sequence just gave two Rectangles in a row, so a Square completes the group.
quests.funFact: Spotting the repeating group is the fastest way to solve any shape pattern.

quests.instruction: Heart, Star, Star, Heart, Star, Star, Heart, Star, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Star
quests.hint: Break this into groups of Heart, Star, Star to spot what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Heart, Star, Star. The sequence just gave Heart, Star — so the group finishes with one more Star.
quests.funFact: Counting carefully through each repeating group helps you never lose track of a pattern.

quests.instruction: Triangle, Triangle, Triangle, Square, Triangle, Triangle, Triangle, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of four: Triangle, Triangle, Triangle, Square — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Triangle, Triangle, Triangle, Square, so after three triangles comes another triangle to start the next group.
quests.funFact: Longer repeating groups take more careful counting, but the same trick still works.

quests.instruction: Square, Triangle, Circle, Square, Triangle, Circle, Square, Triangle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of three: Square, Triangle, Circle — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Square, Triangle, Circle, so after Square, Triangle comes Circle again.
quests.funFact: A three-shape repeating pattern comes back around to the start every third shape.

quests.instruction: Which shape has fewer lines of symmetry than a rectangle, even though both have at least one?
quests.question: Heart
quests.hint: Think about the shape with just a single line of symmetry, fewer than a rectangle's two.
quests.explanation: A heart has just 1 line of symmetry, fewer than a rectangle's 2.
quests.funFact: Even with just one line of symmetry, a heart's matching halves are easy to spot.

quests.instruction: Pentagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, Pentagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, Pentagon, Pentagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Hexagon
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of three: Pentagon, Pentagon, Hexagon — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Pentagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, so after two pentagons comes a hexagon.
quests.funFact: Counting each shape carefully helps you avoid mixing up the order in a repeating group.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 8 lines of symmetry, matching its 8 equal sides?
quests.question: Octagon
quests.hint: Think about the shape with more lines of symmetry than any other polygon you've learned.
quests.explanation: A regular octagon has exactly 8 lines of symmetry, matching its 8 equal sides.
quests.funFact: Among the polygons in this game, an octagon has the most lines of symmetry of all.

quests.instruction: Which shape has only 2 lines of symmetry, just like a rectangle, even though it curves smoothly with no corners?
quests.question: Oval
quests.hint: Think about the round-but-stretched shape you can fold in half only two ways.
quests.explanation: An oval has only 2 lines of symmetry — straight through the middle the long way and the short way.
quests.funFact: A circle has infinite lines of symmetry, but stretching it into an oval reduces that down to just 2.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 5 lines of symmetry, matching its 5 equal sides?
quests.question: Pentagon
quests.hint: Think about the shape with the same number of fold-lines as it has sides, one more than a square.
quests.explanation: A regular pentagon has exactly 5 lines of symmetry, each running from one corner to the middle of the opposite side.
quests.funFact: This pattern — lines of symmetry matching the number of sides — continues for hexagons and octagons too.

quests.instruction: Cone, Cone, Pyramid, Cone, Cone, Pyramid, Cone, Cone, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Pyramid
quests.hint: Break this into groups of Cone, Cone, Pyramid to spot what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Cone, Cone, Pyramid. The sequence just gave two Cones in a row, so a Pyramid completes the group.
quests.funFact: Even with solid shapes, breaking the pattern into its repeating group makes it easy to solve.

quests.instruction: Octagon, Square, Octagon, Square, Octagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Look at how Octagon and Square keep taking turns — which one comes right after Octagon?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Octagon, Square. The sequence just ended on Octagon, so Square comes next.
quests.funFact: No matter how many sides a shape has, it can still take turns in a simple alternating pattern.

quests.instruction: Diamond, Star, Diamond, Star, Diamond, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Star
quests.hint: Follow the back-and-forth between Diamond and Star to find what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Diamond, Star, so after Diamond comes Star again.
quests.funFact: Pointy shapes like diamonds and stars make fun, eye-catching patterns.

quests.instruction: Circle, Square, Triangle, Circle, Square, Triangle, Circle, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Circle, Square, Triangle over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Circle, Square, Triangle, so after Circle, Square comes Triangle again.
quests.funFact: This is one of the most classic three-shape patterns used in early shape learning.

quests.instruction: Circle, Circle, Circle, Square, Circle, Circle, Circle, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of four: Circle, Circle, Circle, Square — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Circle, Circle, Circle, Square, so after Square, a new group starts with Circle again.
quests.funFact: Longer repeating groups just mean counting a bit further before the pattern starts over.

quests.instruction: Sphere, Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Cylinder, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Cone
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Sphere, Cylinder, Cone over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Sphere, Cylinder, Cone. The sequence just gave Sphere, Cylinder — so Cone completes the group.
quests.funFact: Once you spot the repeating trio, you can predict any position in a long pattern.
